title: Advancing brain organoids from disease phenotypes to mechanisms and translation across developmental, infectious, and neurodegenerative diseases
title_zh: 推动脑类器官从疾病表型到发育性、感染性和神经退行性疾病中的机制及转化应用
abstract: Diseases of the central nervous system remain among the greatest unmet medical challenges. Human brain organoids provide 3D multicellular systems for investigating neurodevelopmental, infectious, and neurodegenerative diseases in a human cellular context. Considering these distinct disease areas together highlights how organoid studies are moving beyond recapitulating disease phenotypes to define molecular and cellular mechanisms and trajectories: when pathogenic changes emerge, how they evolve, which cell types and states drive or resist disease, and how multicellular interactions shape progression. Integrating human genetics with longitudinal, single-cell, multi-omic, and functional analyses provides access to human-specific processes that are difficult to capture in animal models and enables identification of mechanisms and therapeutic targets anchored in human disease biology. Increasingly, well-characterized organoids offer human new approach methodologies (NAMs) for preclinical therapeutic evaluation. Advances in reproducibility, benchmarking, and appropriate validation will be critical to establishing their predictive value and supporting their use in drug development and regulatory applications.
abstract_zh: 中枢神经系统疾病仍然是重大未满足的医学挑战。人脑类器官为在人类细胞背景下研究神经发育性、感染性和神经退行性疾病提供了三维多细胞系统。将这些不同疾病领域放在一起考虑，突显了类器官研究如何超越疾病表型的复刻，定义分子和细胞机制及轨迹：致病性变化何时出现、如何演变、哪些细胞类型和状态驱动或抵抗疾病，以及多细胞相互作用如何塑造病程。将人类遗传学与纵向、单细胞、多组学和功能分析相结合，为难以在动物模型中捕获的人类特异性过程提供了途径，并能够识别根植于人类疾病生物学的机制和治疗靶点。经过良好表征的类器官越来越多地提供人体新方法论（NAMs）用于临床前治疗评估。可重复性、基准测试和适当验证的进展对于确立其预测价值并支持其在药物开发和监管申请中的使用将至关重要。
